svg.title: Voltstream: one simulated day, from reading to final bill
svg.desc: Sequence diagram of one simulated day D, which lasts 300 real seconds. In a loop every 2 real seconds meter-producer publishes 50 readings to Kafka. raw-archiver appends them to Parquet in MinIO and speed-layer upserts provisional figures into Postgres every 10 seconds, priced with the previous day's tariff, so the API answers a bill request with the speed row marked provisional. At T+5:00, simulated midnight, reference-dropper writes tariff_D.csv. Within a minute Airflow's tariff_watcher triggers daily_billing, which waits for the file, waits 90 seconds for late readings, then marks pipeline_runs running, rescans the day, and in one transaction replaces the bills and marks the run success. On an exception the run is marked failed and retried twice. Verification, zone rollup, reconciliation and the report follow. From the success commit on, the API serves the batch row as final.
svg.text: 2 · One simulated day: when a bill becomes final
T is real time since day D began; one simulated day = 300 s real (time_scale 288). Numbered steps are referenced by diagrams 3 and 5.
[every 2 s real · 150 ticks per simulated day]
[continuous · each query resumes from its own checkpoint]
success row for D? no → household_running_rt
T+5:00 · simulated midnight: D closes, D+1 begins (both loops carry on for D+1)
meanwhile: F6 backfill for sim_date=D still landing (≤ 30 s)
one transaction: demote old success · replace household_bill_daily
pipeline_runs ← failed · DockerOperator retries 2 (30 s, exponential)
success row for D? yes → household_bill_daily
